**Finding: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data)**

The IP allocation sits in §7.0 Materials:

- **§7.a** — Materials default to **Type II** (IBM-owned) if not expressly designated, so undesignated work product created for us becomes IBM property.
- **§7.c** — the Type II licence back is irrevocable/worldwide/paid-up but limited to distribution "within Customer's Enterprise only" and omits modification, derivative works and sublicensing. That falls short of the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, **modify and sublicense** deliverables for our business).
- No provision anywhere confirms we retain ownership of our Content/data (§11.6 only imposes responsibility; §14.18 addresses contact data only).

IBM's retained ownership of the Base Components (§12.1, §12.3) is acceptable and left untouched.

Redline (validated, ok:true): flip the §7.a default to Type I, broaden the §7.c licence to permit modification and sublicensing for our business purposes, and add a new §7.e confirming our ownership of Content and data with no assignment to IBM and no joint ownership.
